A: Most of these rooms' changes sit where neighbours settle borders (T3-010 in 92 per cent of members). They limit the model's arrows into and out of neighbour talk and sparing (A04, A05, A13: negotiation can precede defence, agreements are invoked but contested) and give deals steps and conditions (P08, P16).
B: the call and the April Fools frame reworked

These rooms change how a call is answered and when building follows it (restrict A12, A01, A02; add-step P01), and how the sub's April Fools frame is tested, policed and ended (add-step and add-condition on K01). Calls to place (T3-002) are three and a half times as common in their changes as in the population's.
C: space and exchange between rooms reworked: spots lost, chosen or yielded, truces and help traded

Half of these rooms' changes sit in the order between rooms. They link the move back to building (P03), limit the move after judging too few hands (A10), and change how a spot is chosen, yielded or lost (Territoriality in 60 per cent of members); the larger half also trades help and agrees truces (Reciprocity).
D: the template and the progress report reworked

These rooms change the model where members share coordinates, templates and how-to (T3-070) and report the mark's state (T3-038): a template does not settle the design (restrict A11), it needs upkeep of its own (add-step P04), and a report can come before the call or the upkeep.
E: the design reworked: what the mark shows argued, sized and taken into chat

These rooms change the model where the mark's design is settled (Collective representation in 83 per cent of members): the design is argued and sized to the hands (add-step and add-condition on P02), a template does not settle it (restrict A11), and planning moves into a chat (P23).
F: keeping reworked: defence and repair under conditions

These rooms change the model where the work is watched, repaired and defended (Repair work in 90 per cent of members): keeping gains conditions and steps (add-condition and add-step on P05), the move after too few hands is limited (restrict A10), and part of the keeping is arranged in a chat (P23).
G: machine hands reworked: scripts installed, kept on target and argued over

Running scripts for the work (T3-028) is in 95 per cent of these rooms. They give the machine hands steps and conditions (add-step and add-condition on P14) and limit the arrow from strained upkeep to scripts (restrict A06).
H: the marking and the record reworked, in rooms that change little else

These rooms make few changes (median 3), and most of them sit at the close: celebrating, crediting and recording the work (Imprinting holds 69 per cent of their changes, against 15 in the population; add-step and link on P11 and P12, restrict A07 and A08).
